# 4 Maccabees Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Brothers' Inner Resolve and Praise

---

**1** For the contest they were engaged in was truly divine, and the virtue being tested was the virtue of endurance.

**2** The prizes they were competing for were incorruptible — prizes of immortality and everlasting glory.

**3** But even if none of those prizes had existed — even if the law had offered no rewards — their reason alone would have been sufficient to earn them the crown of virtue.

**4** They suffered for virtue's sake, and they conquered the tyrant through the power of reason.

**5** The seven brothers are more admirable than the greatest heroes — for they mastered passion not with iron weapons but with the weapons of noble reason.

**6** They surpassed even the heroes of Thermopylae — for those Spartans fought with weapons of iron, but these men fought with the weapons of reason and virtue.

**7** Noble Eleazar was their first champion in battle, the mother of the seven was their second in command, and the seven brothers were their sacred company.

**8** The tyrant was their enemy, the world was their arena, and devotion to God was their weapon.

**9** Their praise has gone out into all the world, for they lived by virtue and died for the law.

**10** In dying for righteousness, they gained life and fame that will never end.

**11** They proved that reason is truly master of the passions — not just in theory but in the reality of their deaths.

**12** They showed that true piety is unbreakable when pushed to the absolute limit.

**13** O mother, what words can do you justice? You bore witness to the faithfulness of the law in your very body.

**14** By your own death you sealed the proof that reason is master of the passions.

**15** Like a wrestler in the arena, you endured every blow of the tyrant's passion and were never knocked down.

**16** You held firm. You did not waver. In your very flesh you proved the sovereignty of reason over passion.

**17** For as long as our nation endures, the memory of Eleazar and the seven brothers and their mother will be imperishable.

**18** Happy are they who received this honor! For they are now at rest with God and with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

**19** The blessed ones proved by the nobility of their dying that reason can master the passions.

**20** I conclude my argument here: devotion to God, guided by reason, is sovereign over all the passions.

**21** This is proved by the heroic deaths of Eleazar and the seven brothers and the mother who was worthy of them all.

**22** Let no one despise old age or youth in matters of virtue — for these heroes prove that neither is an obstacle to virtue.
